To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

BareDroid is a system that allows to analyze Android apps directly on physical devices, and it can be deployed at scale, with a financial investment of only twice the cost of an emulator-based system.

1) we propose a novel system to analyze Android apps on bare metal, which is not detected by malware as an emulated environment and is not detected by emulator-aware heuristics; 2) the cost of BareDroid is less than twice that of emulators, making bare-metal analysis feasible at large-scale; and 3) we open-source BareDroid, in the hope that it can be useful as a tool to strengthen other researchers' analysis systems.

(a) BareDroid is a system that can restore a physical Android device to a clean state in 5.7 minutes, and (b) BareDroid can analyze an order-of-magnitude more apps than an emulator, and is not detected by emulator-aware malware.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two aspects: 1) the design and implementation of BareDroid, and 2) the evaluation of the effectiveness of BareDroid in comparison with an emulator-based system.

(a) showing how BareDroid makes it possible to analyze apps on bare metal, at scale; (b) providing evidence that BareDroid is undetectable to malware and heuristics from previous research; and (c) releasing the BareDroid source code, in order to help other researchers to strengthen the analysis of Android apps.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
BareDroid is the first system that makes bare metal analysis of Android applications on real devices at scale feasible.
BareDroid is a system that makes it feasible to analyze Android apps directly on bare-metal at scale, and that is not detected as emulated by emulator-aware malware.
BareDroid allows to perform analysis of Android applications on real devices, which is not feasible using emulators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a novel system that allows researchers to perform large-scale analysis of Android apps on real devices, without the need to invest in additional hardware, and we release the system as open source.
BareDroid is a system that can be deployed in the wild to analyze apps on real devices at scale.
BareDroid can help the security community to analyze more apps at scale, and to better understand their malicious behavior, by using a more realistic environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time it takes to restore a device is the main obstacle to performing analysis at scale.
, while it is not possible to completely replace the convenience of emulators with real devices, it is possible to make the tradeoff more acceptable, by making bare metal analysis more efficient.
bare-metal analysis is not only possible, but can be done at a cost comparable to that of emulators.
